item.title: MHA directs new protocols on singing Vande Mataram: All six stanzas must be sung
item.description: Govt has issued comprehensive guidelines on singing the National Song, Vande Mataram, mandating the full six-stanza official version at all official events and in schools, and requiring it to be sung before the National Anthem. The post MHA directs new protocols on singing Vande Mataram: All six stanzas must be sung appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Technical objections can’t defeat Covid-19 compensation to Frontline Municipal Worker’s Family; Bombay HC directs immediate release of ₹50 Lakh ex-gratia benefits
item.description: “In such trying times when the employee contracted Covid, to expect him to be admitted only in a government hospital for claiming an entitlement, is arbitrary and unjust.” The post Technical objections can’t defeat Covid-19 compensation to Frontline Municipal Worker’s Family; Bombay HC directs immediate release of ₹50 Lakh ex-gratia benefits appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Remuneration of Junior Resident Doctors qualifies as “salary” for EWS quota eligibility: Delhi HC upholds cancellation of AIIMS Doctor’s appointment
item.description: “The fact that the remuneration was reflected in the pay slips as ‘gross salary’, subjected to statutory tax deductions and reported through Form-16, fortifies the conclusion that the payment was compensatory in nature and not a scholarship granted solely to defray educational expenses.” The post Remuneration of Junior Resident Doctors qualifies as “salary” for EWS quota eligibility: Delhi HC upholds cancellation of AIIMS Doctor’s appointment appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Delhi HC protects Legitimate Expectation of Class XII 2025 Batch Students; holds retrospective withdrawal of additional subject facility by CBSE as arbitrary
item.description: “The petitioners acted in accordance with the existing Bye Laws and the consistent past practice of CBSE and, therefore, had a legitimate expectation that after passing Class XII examination on 13.05.2025 the right to appear as private candidates for the Additional Subject examination, would be available.” The post Delhi HC protects Legitimate Expectation of Class XII 2025 Batch Students; holds retrospective withdrawal of additional subject facility by CBSE as arbitrary appeared first on SCC Tim

item.description: “In normal circumstances and in a suit filed by the plaintiff, it is the plaintiff who has to do the above work and file the documents along with his plaint.” The post Madras High Court orders MS Dhoni to pay Rs 10 lakh towards translation of CDs in Rs 100 crore IPL betting defamation suit appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: GREF Overseer services at Indo-China Border falls under Armed Forces, not Workmen: Punjab and Haryana HC
item.description: “The instant case cannot be termed as a ‘simple accident’ as is understood in common parlance, however, it definitely falls within the definition of ‘accident’ under Rule 3 (1) (ii) of the EOP Rules, which covers within its ambit a mishap due to an act of devotion to duty in an emergency arising otherwise than by violence out of and in the course of service.” The post GREF Overseer services at Indo-China Border falls under Armed Forces, not Workmen: Punjab and Haryana HC appeared first on SCC Ti

item.title: Sections 151 and 152 CPC applies only to clerical or arithmetical error, not merit-based determinations: Kerala HC
item.description: “Clerical mistakes are those that occur in the course of typing or writing, while arithmetical mistakes are those that occur during calculation. As to accidental slip or omission, the decisive test is whether it is apparent from the record that the Court intended to do something but failed to do so owing to an accidental or inadvertent omission.” The post Sections 151 and 152 CPC applies only to clerical or arithmetical error, not merit-based determinations: Kerala HC appeared first on SCC Times

item.title: Suspicion, however grave, can never substitute legal proof: Jammu and Kashmir HC sets aside forgery conviction
item.description: The appeal claims the Trial Court wrongly convicted the appellant because the evidence was weak and misapplied. No selection committee members testified, no forged documents were recovered, and no witness confirmed that the appellant misused his position for promotions. The post Suspicion, however grave, can never substitute legal proof: Jammu and Kashmir HC sets aside forgery conviction appeared first on SCC Times.
